title: An Almost-Linear Approximation Scheme for Edit Distance
main_claim: For every fixed rational ε∈(0,1), a single uniform randomized algorithm approximates the unit-cost edit distance of two strings of total length N within a factor 1+ε with probability ≥ 2/3, in worst-case expected time N^{1+o(1)} on a log-word RAM. It returns 0 deterministically on equal strings. The thresholds are astronomical (exact DP is used unless ℓ ≥ 2^1000, ℓ ≈ log log N).

issues.description: Not an error. The result is purely asymptotic: the fast branch only runs when ℓ ≥ 2^1000 and H ≥ 2^{ℓ/2}, so it needs N roughly 2^{2^{2^{999}}}. The N^{o(1)} overhead decays extremely slowly: the work exponent has o(H) terms like H·q*^2/log ℓ with q* ~ (log ℓ)^{1/4}. The paper says this openly; flagged only so the claim is not read as practical.
issues.evidence: Sec 2: exact DP if ℓ<2^1000 or ℓε<10; Sec 10: q*K_dep log H = O(H q*^2/log ℓ) = o(H), using q*^2 = O(sqrt(log ℓ)).

coverage:
Read all ten sections in full and checked them line by line.
- Seed (Sec 3): shift-tree upper and lower bounds (DFS jump-counting argument, alignment-anchored shift assignment); precision-sampling sandwich and the Bernstein exponents (λQ0/12 = H^3/768); union count; the expected cost E[k/a_w] ≤ H^{8r} with H^{8D0} = 2^{o(H)}; the factor (25+16BH)c ≤ A_init·c.
- Cones (Sec 4): the arithmetic in initial-cone and cone-locality (Fc+66Fb/P ≤ 2Fc, center distance c/16, scale windows).
- Bands (Sec 5): band diameter via the (1-τ)-contraction; rounded-action bounds; one-group Bernstein (ℓ^37/3000) and e* ≤ κδ.
- Comparison tree (Sec 6): the mass telescope (R, G, R±); the energy telescope, including the 3e + 2R_- step; the curvature total; band coverage, where (M/b)(sqrt(KW)+2G) ≤ ℓ^{-44} follows from ℓ^200 ≤ H^{1/100}; the h_Σ guard.
- Regret (Sec 7): the entropy/OFTRL lemma (potential increments, the block-constant μ trick, e^{(1-2κ)x} ≤ 1+(1-κ)x, the 2κ loss); within-block range 3δ ≤ κ/η; the first-crossing clipping argument, both before and after t×, including the failure-event charge.
- Accuracy (Sec 8): the clipped telescope; each term of the total error in eq. 8.1 (2J/S = 200ℓ; bracket terms 51200(p*+21)/ℓ^2 etc.), all < 1/ℓ; Markov plus median amplification (2^{H^2}ℓ^{-H^2/2}); the pass count; the final failure probability < 1/5.
- Numerics (Sec 9): Frank-Wolfe recursion and the smoothing error; strong concavity giving ℓ1 ≤ H^{-3}; the log-series truncation; the exact mixture weights 2(j+1)/(K(K+1)).
- Work (Sec 10): the current-index budget (the |z| ≤ 2h guard gives θ^{-2}(1+b/h) rounded states, which cancels k_h ~ Q1 M h/b); the earlier-input count H^{O(p*)}; local enumeration 2^{O(M p* ℓ)} = 2^{o(H)}; dependency-path count with K_dep = O(H q*/(ℓ log ℓ)); the final sum Σ_j M^j(1+n_x/M^j).
Conditioning and independence (child tables vs. parent streams) were also checked.
The cited external results (Bernstein, Jaggi's FW rate, Pinsker/strong concavity) are applied under their correct hypotheses. No Python check was needed: the parameter inequalities hold by wide margins in log scale.
